docs.text: All notable changes to Skytwin are listed here. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and versions follow Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• skytwin --version prints the version, for bug reports.
  • Training labels: every star, streak and target in the truth carries a label with its drawn path, matched-filter and peak signal-to-noise ratios against the frame's noise, extent above the noise and saturation. Rendered pixels are unchanged.
  • skytwin-export writes YOLO, YOLO-OBB and COCO training sets with tiling, a signal-to-noise threshold and a noise-normalised asinh stretch; skytwin.labels holds the conversions, and skytwin.torch gains detection_target and collate for batching frames with different numbers of objects. See docs/labels.md.
  • examples/track-rate.json: tracking a GEO satellite at its rate from a 790 km orbit through the example profile, so the stars trail into streaks and the satellite stays a point.
  • Rendering: point stars with a pixel-integrated Gaussian PSF, satellite streaks, FITS output (u16, i16, i32 or f32) and a truth file for every frame.
  • Sky: UCAC4 and CSV (Gaia) catalogues with proper motion and parallax; TAN and TAN-SIP WCS; stellar aberration and solar light deflection; passbands with AB zeropoints and colour terms.
  • Time and orbits: UTC/TT with leap seconds; observers and targets from TLEs (SGP4), state vectors or ephemeris tables; Earth shadow and occultation; Lambertian and faceted targets with glints and tumbling; Earthshine and Moonshine; target tracking.
  • Instrument profiles: processing, read-out noise, serial lag, fixed and smooth background fields, per-frame sky light, temperature and dark current, hot and flickering pixels, radiation hits with a rate map, CTI, PSF wings, Moffat tail and field variation, smear, bleeding, serial overflow, flat field with vignetting, PRNU, dust and field stop, radial lens distortion, pointing motion and header pointing errors, stray light, zodiacal light, chip layout and instrument-style headers, read-out faults.
  • Curved drift and image roll during the exposure (pointing.drift_turn_deg_per_s, roll_rate_deg_per_s, roll_centre_px): stars trail in arcs, and the reported roll follows the image.
  • Profiles as contracts: schema_version, sensor, learned provenance and the catalog a profile was calibrated against; scenes give only the catalogue's path.
  • Sequences, only_visible target filtering, and batches for training sets on all cores; per-pixel random streams for exact clean/dirty pairs.
  • Truth: Cramér–Rao bounds, trail ends, light curves, photon counts.
  • A provenance manifest for every run.
  • The skytwin Python package streaming frames to numpy and PyTorch.
  • skytwin-calibrate: learns a profile from real frames (headers, noise, photon-transfer gain, serial lag, hot pixels, flat and field stop, PSF, astrometry and distortion from the frames' own WCS, forced-photometry zeropoint and colour term, radiation, stray light, read-out faults), refines it against simulated twins, reports realism, scores detectors, and checks a catalogue against a profile.
  • learn --calibration reads the camera's bias, dark and flat frames for gain, read noise, dark current, radiation rate, read-out time and dust shadows; learn also reads the pixel size from the headers (XPIXSZ and kin).
  • learn handles frames whose stars trail, as when the telescope tracks a satellite: it measures each frame's trail and fits the PSF, zeropoint and radiation around the trails.
  • learn gives ground frames a zeropoint above the atmosphere, fitted against airmass, or moved with --extinction (default 0.2 mag/airmass) when the frames span too little airmass.
  • learn --ephemeris gives spacecraft states and sub-satellite points to frames whose headers carry none, from a CSV or a JPL Horizons vector table.
  • Profiles learned from public archives: profiles/cassiope-fai-nir.json (the DUST dataset), profiles/wise-w1.json (WISE's 3.4 µm band), profiles/astrianet-pl16803.json (a ground camera tracking satellites) and profiles/ckoirama-cdk24.json (a ground 0.6 m telescope). profiles/README.md gives each one's source and how closely its twins match.
  • A documentation site built from docs/, versioned with mike, with the command-line reference from --help and the Python API from docstrings.
  • Ground-site observers: a telescope at a WGS84 latitude, longitude and height, turning with the Earth (UT1 = UTC + DUT1), seen through the atmosphere (refraction from pressure and temperature, extinction per airmass, the horizon as the occulting edge); SITELAT, SITELONG, SITEELEV and AIRMASS header keywords and the site and atmosphere in the truth. Example examples/ground-tracks-meo.json.

docs.title: Command-line reference
docs.text: Each command's options and defaults, as printed by its --help option in skytwin 0.1.0. For tasks and examples, see the guides.

docs.title: skytwin
docs.text:
usage: skytwin <scene.json> <out.fits> [--seed N] [--write-flat] [--frames N] [--jobs N] [--compact-truth]
       skytwin --version
Writes <out.fits> and <out>.truth.json.
The scene file may name an instrument profile: "instrument": "profiles/x.json".
--frames N renders N independent frames (a "batch"), on --jobs threads (default: all cores).
--compact-truth writes the truth JSON without indentation (about 30% smaller, faster).

docs.title: skytwin-export
docs.text:
usage: skytwin-export [-h] [--frames FRAMES] [--start START] [--seed SEED]
                      [--format {yolo,yolo-obb,coco}] [--classes CLASSES] [--by-form]
                      [--min-snr MIN_SNR] [--min-visible MIN_VISIBLE] [--min-radius MIN_RADIUS]
                      [--streak-px STREAK_PX] [--tile TILE] [--overlap OVERLAP] [--val VAL]
                      [--image {asinh,raw16}] [--workers WORKERS] [--keep-truth] [--overwrite]
                      scene out

Render frames of a Skytwin scene into a YOLO or COCO training set.

positional arguments:
  scene                 scene file (JSON)
  out                   output folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --frames FRAMES       frames to render (default: the scene's batch.frames, else 1)
  --start START         first frame index (default 0)
  --seed SEED           replace the scene's seed
  --format {yolo,yolo-obb,coco}
                        label format, repeatable (default yolo); yolo and yolo-obb share labels/,
                        so pick one
  --classes CLASSES     kinds to label, separated by commas: star, satellite or star,satellite
                        (default)
  --by-form             split each kind into _point and _streak classes
  --min-snr MIN_SNR     least matched-filter signal-to-noise (default 5)
  --min-visible MIN_VISIBLE
                        least share of a point's box in a tile (0.5)
  --min-radius MIN_RADIUS
                        least box half-width before the half pixel, px (default FWHM)
  --streak-px STREAK_PX
                        least span of a streak's path, px (default 2 × FWHM)
  --tile TILE           cut frames into tiles of this many pixels
  --overlap OVERLAP     least overlap between tiles, px (default 0)
  --val VAL             share of frames for validation (default 0.1)
  --image {asinh,raw16}
                        image encoding (default asinh)

usage: skytwin-calibrate [-h]
                         {learn,check,describe,measure,psf,profile,refine,twins,report,score} ...

positional arguments:
  {learn,check,describe,measure,psf,profile,refine,twins,report,score}
    learn               learn a whole profile from sample frames, in one step
    check               check a local star catalogue against what a profile was calibrated with
    describe            what a profile is, what it needs, and a scene to start from
    measure             per-frame statistics of real or simulated frames
    psf                 stack isolated stars and fit a multi-Gaussian PSF
    profile             build profile blocks from statistics
    refine              simulate, measure and correct a profile in place
    twins               simulate twins of real frames and measure them
    report              compare real and simulated statistics
    score               score a detector's source list against a truth file

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

docs.title: skytwin-calibrate learn
docs.text:
usage: skytwin-calibrate learn [-h] -o OUT [--keywords KEYWORDS] [--skytwin SKYTWIN]
                               [--ucac4 UCAC4] [--catalog CATALOG] [--catalog-name CATALOG_NAME]
                               [--catalog-source CATALOG_SOURCE] [--sensor-name SENSOR_NAME]
                               [--platform PLATFORM] [--band-nm FROM TO] [--ephemeris EPHEMERIS]
                               [--extinction EXTINCTION] [--pixel-pitch-um PIXEL_PITCH_UM]
                               [--calibration CALIBRATION [CALIBRATION ...]] [--fayde FAYDE]
                               [--max-frames MAX_FRAMES] [--iterations ITERATIONS] [--twins TWINS]
                               [--work WORK]
                               inputs [inputs ...]

positional arguments:
  inputs                directories, FITS files, glob patterns or .txt lists

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -o, --out OUT         profile to write (a .learn.md report and .keywords.json go beside it)
  --keywords KEYWORDS   header keyword map (default: worked out from the headers)
  --skytwin SKYTWIN     skytwin binary: refine the profile and write a realism report
  --ucac4 UCAC4         UCAC4 directory: plate solves for scale, parity and header pointing
                        errors, and real-sky twins
  --catalog CATALOG     star catalogue for matching, photometry and real-sky twins instead of
                        --ucac4: a UCAC4 directory or a CSV (Gaia extract, Skytwin column names).
                        Use one with good photometry for the stars the camera sees: UCAC4's own
                        magnitudes saturate brighter than about 8
  --catalog-name CATALOG_NAME
                        name recorded for the catalogue in the profile (default: the file name)
  --catalog-source CATALOG_SOURCE
                        how to get or rebuild the catalogue, recorded in the profile
  --sensor-name SENSOR_NAME
                        sensor name recorded in the profile (default: INSTRUME/TELESCOP)
  --platform PLATFORM   spacecraft or mission recorded in the profile
  --band-nm FROM TO     passband recorded in the profile
  --ephemeris EPHEMERIS
                        spacecraft states for frames whose headers carry none: a CSV (time_utc,
                        x_km, y_km, z_km, vx_km_s, vy_km_s, vz_km_s; geocentric GCRS) or a JPL
                        Horizons vector table (geocentric, in km and km/s or in au and au/day)
  --extinction EXTINCTION
                        ground frames: extinction, mag/airmass, to move the zeropoint above the
                        atmosphere when the frames do not span enough airmass to fit it (default
                        0.2)
  --pixel-pitch-um PIXEL_PITCH_UM
                        unbinned pixel size, um, when the headers do not give it (radiation rates
                        per cm² need it)
  --calibration CALIBRATION [CALIBRATION ...]
                        bias, dark and flat frames of the same camera (directories, files, glob
                        patterns or .txt lists): gain, read noise, dark current, cosmic rays and
                        dust shadows from them
  --fayde FAYDE         fayde binary for the plate solves (default: on the PATH)
  --max-frames MAX_FRAMES
                        frames to sample from the inputs (default 1500)
  --iterations ITERATIONS
                        refinement passes (default 2)
  --twins TWINS         simulated twins per refinement pass (default 200); the realism report uses
                        up to 300
  --work WORK           working directory (default: beside the profile)
